back: A broad improvement in well-being: higher incomes, better health and education, less poverty and inequality.
An adjustment converting incomes at the rate that equalises the price of a basket of goods, to compare what incomes can buy.
The geometric mean of the health, education and income indices.

front: Three problems with GDP per head as a measure of living standards?
back: It hides inequality, omits non-market output and the informal sector, and ignores the environment and leisure.

front: What is the **Measure of Economic Welfare (MEW)**?
back: GDP adjusted for leisure and unpaid work and net of environmental and urban costs.
A measure of how many people are deprived in several dimensions of health, education and living standards, and how intensely.
Inequality first rises and then falls as income per head grows (an inverted U); the evidence is mixed.

front: Why is the income index of the HDI logarithmic?
back: Extra income adds less to well-being at higher income levels.
